description: MCP server for stacktr.ee: publish HTML privately from any AI agent (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Claude.ai). Unguessable, replace-in-place URLs, passcodes, and who opened it.

tool_signatures.name: claim_site
tool_signatures.description: Adopt a page that was published without an account into the account this key belongs to. Pass the claim_token from the anonymous publish response. Do this whenever you published anonymously and a key is now available: an unclaimed free page dies at 24 hours, and claiming gives it the longest life the plan allows, never a shorter one, with the same URL, id, token and read history. A claim IS a publish: on a free key it spends one of the three lifetime pages and can return 402 plan_lifetime_limit_exceeded or 429 plan_site_limit_exceeded, and the claim link stays valid until the page expires, so report the wall rather than retrying. A wallet-paid page is the exception: it spends no quota and keeps the permanence it paid for. Claiming SPENDS the claim_token — it stops being the page\

tool_signatures.name: create_client_space
tool_signatures.description: Create a client space before anything is published into it. Rarely needed: publish_html with a client argument auto-creates the space under the same casing and slug rules, so use this only when the user is setting a client up ahead of the work. Idempotent with that auto-create — an existing space matching the name or slug, in any casing, comes back instead of a duplicate. The returned slug is the space’s permanent address segment; a later rename changes the display name only.

tool_signatures.name: create_share_link
tool_signatures.description: Mint a share link addressed to one person. Put their name in label and every open through that link comes back attributed to it, in the dashboard and in the read-receipt email. The link skips the page passcode and can be revoked on its own. One per recipient after publish_html; for a whole mail-merge append ?to={{name}} to the page URL instead.

tool_signatures.name: delete_client_space
tool_signatures.description: Delete a client space. The pages filed under it are NOT deleted: they detach to floating pages and keep working on their existing URLs, so delivered work stays reachable. The space itself goes, and with it the generated portal page and any address connected to it, which stop resolving. A space-level viewer gate goes with the space too: a page that was protected only by the space passcode or email domain, and carries no gate of its own, becomes reachable by anyone holding its link. Warn the user, and set_password on the pages that have to stay private before deleting. When the user means a client is simply finished, prefer update_client_space with archived: true — archiving keeps the portal and the address live, frees the plan slot, and can be undone.

tool_signatures.name: delete_site
tool_signatures.description: Take a page down. The link goes dead immediately for everyone holding it, and the content is kept for 30 days: restore_site puts it back at the same URL, with the same id, token, slug and read history, any time in that window. After the 30 days the content is destroyed and cannot be recovered by anyone. So this is undoable, but it is not a preview: tell the user their link stops working now. On the free plan deleting does not hand back a lifetime page slot, because that cap counts publishes rather than live pages. Deleting a page that is already down is not an error: the response comes back with already_deleted: true and the same restorable_until. Read restorable_until (unix seconds) off the response before promising a restore: it is absent when the delete was not recoverable.

tool_signatures.name: get_approval_status
tool_signatures.description: Where an approval request stands. state is

tool_signatures.name: get_content
tool_signatures.description: Read a page\

tool_signatures.name: get_design_guide
tool_signatures.description: Fetch the Stacktree house design guide for improving a published page. Call this BEFORE any request to make a page look better, more polished, more professional, or

tool_signatures.name: get_me
tool_signatures.description: Who this key publishes as, and what its plan actually allows: plan, signed-in email, pages held, lifetime publishes spent, and a limits object. READ limits RATHER THAN QUOTING NUMBERS FROM ANY OTHER TOOL DESCRIPTION — those describe the free plan and this key may be on any plan. Worth calling before promising a permanent link (max_expiry_hours), before promising a passcode or email gate (passwords, email_gates), and after a 402 or 429 so you can say which wall was hit. The email also answers

tool_signatures.name: get_passcode
tool_signatures.description: Show the passcode set on a page this account owns, so it can be sent to the client again. Works for passcodes set since 13 September 2026 (kept as an encrypted copy beside the hash the gate checks). An older one answers not_retrievable: the page still asks for it, and the fix is set_password with a new one, then send that.

tool_signatures.name: get_revision_brief
tool_signatures.description: Everything that came back on one page, as the brief for its next version: the reviewer\

tool_signatures.name: get_site
tool_signatures.description: Read the current HTML source of a site you own, so you can edit it and update_site in place. Returns the exact stored index.html (not rendered or text-stripped), preserving CSS and inline charts.

tool_signatures.name: link_wallet
tool_signatures.description: Link your wallet to a Stacktree account so the pages you publish are owned there — and adopt the ones you already published. Get a LINK-XXXX code from your human (generated at stacktr.ee/wallets). First call with just { code } to get the exact message to sign; sign it with your wallet (personal_sign / EIP-191); then call again with { code, wallet, signature }.

tool_signatures.name: list_client_spaces
tool_signatures.description: List the client spaces on this account: slug, name, page_count, last activity, hostname (the space’s own address, e.g. acme.theiragency.com, when one is connected) and portal_enabled (whether the space serves a generated client portal at that address). Spaces group published pages per client (

tool_signatures.name: list_feedback
tool_signatures.description: Read viewer feedback left on a site via the Agentation toolbar. Each item has a comment plus the annotated element, selected text, intent and severity; unresolved items first. The loop: list_feedback → get_site/update_site → resolve_feedback.

tool_signatures.name: list_responses
tool_signatures.description: What readers sent through the forms on a page. A form in published HTML marked <form data-stacktree-form=

tool_signatures.name: list_share_links
tool_signatures.description: Share links on a page with attributed opens and last-opened time. opens counts human page opens through that link; use_count is the raw max_uses counter, not a read metric. opens is null on a plan without viewer numbers.

tool_signatures.name: list_sites
tool_signatures.description: List sites owned by this API key. Viewer numbers are plan-gated: when metrics_locked is true, view_count, unique_viewers and last_viewed_at are null and only the boolean opened is meaningful. Report

tool_signatures.name: list_versions
tool_signatures.description: List earlier versions of a page this key owns, newest first. Every update replaces a page in place, and the content it replaced is kept here: one snapshot per update, taken the moment before the new content landed. Call this whenever an update turned out wrong, or the user asks what a page said before, or asks for last month\

tool_signatures.name: open_html_file
tool_signatures.description: The Stacktree viewer for an .html file the user opens in ChatGPT desktop: preview it, publish it to a private link, add a passcode, send it to a named client, and keep the page in sync as the file changes. ChatGPT calls this itself when the user opens the file. A file path does not work here: to publish a file you can read, call publish_html with its contents.

tool_signatures.name: publish_card_open
tool_signatures.description: Used by the Stacktree publish card in the chat: a short-lived owner preview link for one page, which opens it without counting as a visit and without asking for its passcode. Read-only. Not a link to send anyone: it stops working after 15 minutes.

tool_signatures.name: publish_card_status
tool_signatures.description: Used by the Stacktree publish card in the chat to refresh itself: the page’s link, whether and by whom it has been opened, its passcode, expiry and client. Read-only. An agent answering the user should use list_sites or list_share_links instead.

tool_signatures.name: publish_html
tool_signatures.description: Turn HTML into a link a person can open in a browser. Reach for this whenever a page you produced has to be seen by someone who is not in this conversation — a client, a teammate, a reviewer, a channel — or when the user says

tool_signatures.name: publish_revision
tool_signatures.description: Publishes the new version of a page that has feedback and resolves the comments it answers, in one step. The HTML is replaced in place, exactly as update_site does (same link, so everyone holding it sees the new version; the old one is kept in list_versions). Then each listed comment is resolved with its note, and one message back to the reviewer is left with them. The reviewer sees the notes and the message next to their comments the next time they open the page. Use it instead of update_site when the new version answers feedback from get_revision_brief. If the update is refused, nothing is resolved.

tool_signatures.name: request_approval
tool_signatures.description: Get a named person\

tool_signatures.name: resolve_addressed_notes
tool_signatures.description: After update_site: resolve the open notes the new version appears to answer (comments whose words are gone, sections that were asked to change and have been edited), with one line each reviewer sees next to their own note. Only notes the update actually touched are resolved. Leave ids out to resolve all of them.

tool_signatures.name: resolve_comments
tool_signatures.description: Resolves several comments on one page in one call, each with a short note, plus one optional message back to the reviewer. For when nothing needs publishing: approvals, or comments an earlier update already answered. The person who left each comment sees the note next to it on the page, so write it to them. Ids that are not open on this page are skipped and reported back.

tool_signatures.name: resolve_feedback
tool_signatures.description: Mark a feedback item as addressed after fixing the page. Optionally include a note describing the change.

tool_signatures.name: restore_site
tool_signatures.description: Put a page back at the same URL after it was deleted or ran out of time. Same id, same token, same slug, same read history, so every link already sent starts working again. Call this, and never publish_html, whenever update_site, set_expiry, set_password or another settings call answers 409 site_deleted: publishing the page again mints a different URL, strands everyone holding the old one, and spends another of the free plan\

tool_signatures.name: restore_version
tool_signatures.description: Put an earlier version of a page back at the same URL, after a bad update. Get the version id from list_versions first. Same link, same id, same read history, so nothing needs re-sending. This is NOT restore_site: restore_site brings back a page that was DELETED or expired, this rolls a live page\

tool_signatures.name: revoke_share_link
tool_signatures.description: Kill one share link. The page and every other link keep working — cut off one recipient without re-issuing to the rest.

tool_signatures.name: set_client
tool_signatures.description: File an existing site under a client space (by name or slug, auto-created), or pass client: null to detach it to a floating page. Mirrors set_password: one site, one call.

tool_signatures.name: set_client_feedback
tool_signatures.description: Switch how the people you send a page to can answer on it, with no account. comments: they select words, or click an image, video or section, and leave a comment only the owner sees (read them with list_feedback, fix with update_site, then resolve_feedback with a note the client sees). reactions: one-tap emoji. Pass either or both; omitted ones are left as they are.

tool_signatures.name: set_email_gate
tool_signatures.description: Restrict viewer access to a specific email domain (strict-equal match). Viewers must verify via a one-time magic link. Mutually exclusive with set_password. Pass domain: null to clear. Email gates are a paid feature: on a free key, setting one returns 402 plan_viewer_gate_not_available.

tool_signatures.name: set_expiry
tool_signatures.description: Set hours-from-now expiry, or null for never. A NUMBER above the plan ceiling is shortened to it (free: 168 hours) and the response says so. null on a plan that caps page lifetime is REFUSED — 409 expiry_clamped, nothing changed — rather than quietly becoming 7 days, so a shortened page can never be reported as permanent: either resend with accept_clamp: true to take the ceiling, or tell the user the plan cannot make this link permanent. Quote expires_at_iso from the response, never the value you asked for.

tool_signatures.name: set_password
tool_signatures.description: Set or clear (null) a passcode on a site. Works on every plan, free keys included. Clearing one always works.

tool_signatures.name: stacktree_pages
tool_signatures.description: Lists the pages you have published on Stacktree, newest first, with their links, viewers and expiry.

tool_signatures.name: unopened_pages
tool_signatures.description: The pages, and the named people, that have not opened what was sent to them an hour after it went up, newest first. Most pages are opened within the hour they are sent, so one that is still quiet has usually not gone out: hand the person their link again (each item carries it), or ask your user who an unnamed page is for and call whos_it_for. Read-only.

tool_signatures.name: update_client_space
tool_signatures.description: Rename a client space, archive or unarchive it, or set the viewer gate that covers every page in the space. Omit a field to leave it untouched. A rename changes the display name only — the slug is a permanent addressing contract and never moves. Archiving frees the space’s plan slot and closes its portal and connected address to readers (they see a

tool_signatures.name: update_site
tool_signatures.description: Replace the HTML of an existing site in place. The URL stays the same, so everyone you already sent it to sees the new version without being sent anything. Use this — not another publish_html — every time you revise a page you have already published: iterating with publish_html strands the link people are holding on the old version and burns a page slot. The PII pre-flight scan runs on the new content too (MCP default: block; pass pii_check:

tool_signatures.name: whos_it_for
tool_signatures.description: Record who a published page is for, by name, and get back that person’s own link to hand over. Ask your user who the page is for before you hand a link over, then call this once per person. Every open through the link comes back with their name, and if they have not opened it an hour after it went up, the owner’s dashboard says so. It records only: nothing is sent to anyone. Unlike create_share_link, the link keeps the page’s passcode or email gate in front of it. To file the page under the person’s company, use set_client.
